title: Skeleton's specification sends a consumer to the wrong stylesheet
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, one of three asked whether each component specification still describes the component that exists

evidence.verified: `grep -rn cs-skeleton src/styles/` returns only `src/styles/components/skeleton.css`, which `src/styles/components.css:29` imports, and `src/styles/base.css` imports `./reset.css` and nothing else. Both claims in the specification now name that file. `npm run check` exits 0.

details:
`components/Skeleton.md:73` says the `cs-skeleton` class is defined in `src/styles/base.css`, and `:51` says no separate import is needed when `base.css` is already imported.

The class is defined at `src/styles/components/skeleton.css:1` and reaches a consumer through `src/styles/components.css:29`. `src/styles/base.css` imports `reset.css` and nothing else.

A consumer who follows the specification and imports `base.css` alone gets an unstyled, unanimated `<span>`, with no error and no warning.

That is the failure mode recorded in CUI-006, arriving through the documentation rather than through a guess.

notes.text: Session agent confirmed every citation in this record against the tree at a374f2c before filing it.

A documentation fix rather than a code one: the stylesheet is where it belongs, and the specification pointed somewhere else. Nothing gates a prose claim about which file defines a class, so this can drift again.
